results: 1. Comprehensive movement-disorders examination with observation at rest, during posture and voluntary tasks, distraction, sensory tricks, and assessment for dystonia, tremor, chorea, tics, rigidity, bradykinesia, apraxia, and pyramidal signs
limb power and wasting: mild distal finger muscle wasting
2. Surface electromyography of bilateral forearm and hand muscles during rest, sustained posture, and voluntary movements
surface EMG of forearm flexors and extensors: synchronous discharges at about 8 Hz in both forearm flexors and extensors
3. MRI of the brain with and without contrast
brain MRI: no brain lesion on unenhanced MRI with diffusion imaging
4. Serum ceruloplasmin, serum copper, liver function tests, and 24-hour urinary copper
copper / caeruloplasmin / 24 h urinary copper: normal
5. Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, thyroid-stimulating hormone, vitamin B12, and folate
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
TSH / free T4: normal - not thyrotoxic
vitamin B12 with methylmalonic acid: normal
6. MRI of the cervical spine with and without contrast
cervical spine MRI (including flexion views): ON NECK FLEXION, prominent flow voids in a widened posterior epidural space from C6 to T3 - diagnostic of Hirayama disease
7. Genetic testing for an inherited dystonia syndrome if the movement-disorders examination supports early-onset or familial dystonia
genetic testing (targeted panel or exome): no pathogenic variant
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Hirayama disease (cervical flexion-induced monomelic amyotrophy) caused by dynamic anterior displacement of the posterior dura with cervical spinal cord compression at C6–T3, producing distal hand wasting and an 8-Hz postural tremor

ALTERNATIVE 1: Cortical or segmental myoclonus

ALTERNATIVE 2: Essential postural tremor

ALTERNATIVE 3: Motor neuron disease presenting with distal upper-limb wasting
